concepts.gloss_en: The breath that has no sin in it — the pure/holy breath (of schoolchildren), equated with the air of Eretz Yisrael, in Torah 37

reason_for_human: All six occurrences are the same phrase in Torah 37, referring to the sinless breath of children / air of Eretz Yisrael. The single 'holy' variant (הבל הקדוש) is just the adjective הקדוש inserted into the identical phrase, used interchangeably within the very same paragraph (37_4_2) as the plain form — a descriptive modifier, not a different concept. Same word, same referent throughout, so the round-1 merge stands.
